Gold went nowhere on purpose. On the eve of the Fed's decision, spot held near $4,046 an ounce, coiled inside a $4,021–$4,080 triangle with the market unwilling to move a dollar until Wednesday.

What makes this meeting different: the odds are genuinely split — about 62% for a hold at 3.50–3.75%, a full 38% for a hike, and roughly 81% for a move by September. Q2 GDP and core PCE land Thursday. For the jewelry counter the number that matters isn't the ceiling — it's the floor. Hold $3,964 and gold stays the value story a cautious shopper is already choosing.

Gold got the headlines; the white metals got the money. Palladium jumped about 3.3% to ~$1,268, platinum added 1.7% to ~$1,612, and silver held near $58.50 with $60 back in sight after an intraday $60.11 earlier this month.

The twist: platinum is firm on industrial and investment demand even as its jewelry demand falls 12% this year. Silver is the one the bench feels — a push to $60 lifts every finding and chain, just as gold's price pushes shoppers toward silver in the first place.

Bonhams brought more than 300 jewels to the block in California — and the smallest lots said the most. Three unmounted fancy-color diamonds anchored the sale: a 1.01ct pink-purple oval (~$50k), a 1.64ct deep pink (~$35k) and a 0.53ct heart-shaped blue (~$35k).

The marquee curiosity: a 70-carat diamond necklace carrying a $50k top estimate and offered with no reserve — meaning it sells to the highest bid, however low. No-reserve lots are how a house lets the room, not the estimate, find the price. Watch that necklace for the sale's honest number.
